focus: P2 GraphProjectionReducerV1 event-envelope, replay, checkpoint, point-in-time, rebuild, and audit-preserving compaction contract
noveltyJustification: Repo 1 fixed the authority boundary and named checkpoint fields, but did not close the event/no-op dispatch contract, dual domain/audit replay proof, exact checkpoint acceptance algorithm, inclusive point-in-time semantics, atomic rebuild behavior, or the audit-preserving non-compaction decision.
keyFindings: Consume only fully verified 036 events through exact event-version and reducer-version transitions or registered deterministic no-ops
Treat GraphCheckpointV1 as a discardable exact-prefix proof bound to domain and authorization-audit replay identities
Rebuild from verified history fail-closed, repeat-reduce canonical bytes, and publish only atomically after fingerprint verification
Define point-in-time as an inclusive authoritative sequence fold, optionally accelerated by an exact verified prefix checkpoint
Never physically compact committed 036 domain or authorization-audit events; compact only disposable projections, indexes, caches, checkpoints, or byte-preserving sealed packaging
Bind graph replay to authorization history so equal terminal state cannot conceal denied, unapplied, or differently authorized paths

ruledOut.approach: Delete events when current folds are equivalent
ruledOut.reason: Present-state equivalence destroys point-in-time, authorization, causation, and replay-fingerprint evidence
Authoritative ledger sequence, not wall time, defines admission and causal order
A snapshot does not prove stored/effective history or the replay machinery that produced it
Unversioned filtering changes the committed replay range; omissions require registered deterministic no-ops
